stem: A neutral atom has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. What is its mass number?
Which feature of an atom determines which element it is?
Sodium and potassium are in the same group (column) of the periodic table. Why do they react in similar ways?
options: They have the same number of valence electrons.
They have the same atomic mass.
They have the same number of neutrons.
They have the same number of electron energy levels.

stem: Which of the following is a chemical change?
Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) turns directly into a gas without melting. What is this change called?
Which of the following are physical changes? Select all that apply.
Which set of coefficients balances this equation? __ H₂ + __ O₂ → __ H₂O
What type of reaction is Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂?
In a sealed container, 10 grams of reactants react completely. What is the total mass of the products?
options: Less than 10 grams, because some mass becomes energy
More than 10 grams, because new bonds add mass
It cannot be predicted without the balanced equation

stem: Which change would NOT speed up a chemical reaction?
options: Increasing the concentration of a reactant
Grinding a solid reactant into powder

stem: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It lowers the activation energy needed.
It raises the temperature of the mixture.
It is used up to supply extra energy.
It increases the total amount of product made.

stem: Why does food spoil more slowly in a refrigerator?
options: Cold air contains less oxygen than warm air, so oxidation stops.
Cold temperatures kill the bacteria and molds that make food spoil.
Lower temperature slows particles, so reactions happen more slowly.
The refrigerator removes all moisture, so no reactions can occur.

stem: In salt water, what is the salt?
A red blood cell is placed in a hypertonic solution (one with a higher solute concentration than the cell). What happens to the cell?
options: It takes in salt from the solution and swells.
It shrinks as water leaves it.

stem: How many grams of glucose are in 250 mL of a 5% (weight/volume) glucose solution? Enter a number.
A solution has a pH of 3. How would you describe it?
A solution at pH 4 has how many times the hydrogen ion concentration of a solution at pH 6?
When an acid reacts completely with a base, what are the usual products?
A nurse needs to measure exactly 37 mL of a liquid. Which of these tools gives the most precise measurement?
Convert 2.5 kilograms to grams. Enter a number.
How should you read the volume of water in a graduated cylinder?
options: At the top edge of the curved surface, looking down from above
At the bottom of the curved surface (meniscus), with your eye level with it
At the highest marking on the cylinder that the water touches along the glass
At the average of the top and bottom of the curve, viewed from any angle

stem: A student measures an enzyme's activity. Activity rises steadily from 20 °C to 40 °C, then drops sharply between 40 °C and 50 °C. What is the best prediction for its activity at 60 °C?
options: Very low, because high heat changes the enzyme's shape
Higher than at 40 °C, because heat speeds up reactions
About the same as at 20 °C, because the curve repeats
Twice the activity at 40 °C, because the temperature is higher

stem: A sealed syringe of air is kept at constant temperature. If you push the plunger in so the volume of air decreases, what happens to the pressure of the air?
A study finds that towns with more hospitals also have more deaths each year. What is the best conclusion?
options: Hospitals cause more people to die, so towns should build fewer of them.
More deaths cause towns to build more hospitals to keep up with demand.
The data must contain an error, because hospitals are known to save lives.
They are correlated; a third factor, such as population, may explain both.

stem: Which statement is a testable hypothesis?
options: Plants are the most beautiful living things.
If plants receive more light, then they will grow taller.
The plant grew 5 centimeters last week.
Plants are green because their leaves contain the pigment chlorophyll.

stem: Which statement about a patient is an inference rather than an observation?
options: The patient's skin is red and warm.
The patient probably has an infection.
The patient's heart rate is 110 beats per minute.

stem: Which evidence would best support the claim that Drug X lowers blood pressure?
options: A well-known athlete says Drug X lowered her own blood pressure.
Ten people who already take Drug X say on a survey that they now feel much healthier.
An advertisement from the drug's maker says it is the best treatment.
In a large randomized trial, Drug X lowered pressure more than a placebo did.

stem: A student tests how fertilizer affects plant growth. She gives four groups of plants 0, 5, 10 and 15 grams of fertilizer and measures their height after three weeks. What is the independent variable?
In the same fertilizer experiment, what is the purpose of the group that receives 0 grams of fertilizer?
options: It is the control group for comparison.
It only increases the total sample size.
It proves that the hypothesis is correct.

stem: Put these steps of the scientific method in the usual order.
options: Make an observation and ask a question
